record.chaining: Euro pricing plus crypto is the composition that matters for a registrant without a Russian instrument: a machine in Moscow or Amsterdam at EUR 5.93 a month paid in USDT, with hourly billing for the testing day, and traffic the provider advertises as unlimited, which is the one claim here that would remove the egress ceiling that binds everywhere else.
record.limits_note: Nothing in the published terms binds above the scale: the provider advertises unlimited traffic on 25 Gbit/s links, and the constraint that does exist is commercial rather than technical, because the hourly rate is roughly five times the monthly rate for the same machine.
record.binding_note: the price binds: the smallest orderable shape is over USD 5, so the unlimited traffic never gets used

identity_cost.detail: email plus a robot check at signup, with crypto top-up documented in the vendor wiki; the order console is a separate host (my.aeza.net) that did not render for a text read. No card amount or hold read

record.reliability_note: Aeza Group has been on the US OFAC SDN list since 2025-07-01, so the machine can stop existing for reasons the contract does not cover; its own storefront would not answer through automated retrieval on 2026-10-24.

record.notes: Two prices, two products: EUR 5.93 is the standing plan and EUR 1.99 is a loss-leader described in the wiki with no listed specification. Without the promo's shape the EUR 1.99 claim cannot be ranked, and the promo may be sold out. ⛔ OFAC SDN listed since 2025-07-01. That is a technical reliability fact about continuity, documented because a buyer loses the machine and the balance rather than because of any judgement about the listing. The UK company 15109642 is a shell. The storefront did not answer through automated retrieval on 2026-10-24, so whether it is purchasable today is unverified.

record.notes: EUR 5.93 is USD 6.64, so even the smallest Aéza plan misses the line, and 4 GB is EUR 11.87. The row is documented because unlimited traffic on a 25 Gbit/s port with one IPv4 and a /48 of IPv6 is the most generous network term in evaluated offerings. Aéza's wiki advertises separate 'promo plans' for new customers; they were not listed on this page and are the one place a sub-USD-5 Aéza shape could hide.
